findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MyAccessibilityService.kt findAndClickCloseButton picks the rightmost blank ImageView
findings.claim: The close button is located geometrically as the ImageView with blank contentDescription and text that is farthest right on screen. In the observed popup tree every other icon sits left of its text so the X wins, but a future Picap layout with a right-side icon could be clicked instead. The Aceptar-node guard limits the branch to service popups; if the heuristic misclicks the worst case is a harmless tap and a log line, and the log records the chosen bounds for diagnosis.

findings.claim: Non-Cruz-Verde detection reuses servicio, which only matches a non-address node containing cruz verde. If Picap ever renders a genuine Cruz Verde order whose only Cruz Verde text is the pickup or delivery address, servicio would be empty and the popup would be auto-closed as non-CV. This matches the reported behavior today (CV orders carry an isolated Cruz Verde service label) and the maintainer rule that absence of that node means not Cruz Verde, so the risk is accepted; the NO-CV log line makes any misclassification visible in logcat.

findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MyAccessibilityService.kt NO-CV branch runs before the auto-accept switch check
findings.claim: The close action is unconditional per the explicit request: non-CV popups are dismissed even when the Picap auto-accept master switch is off, so a user browsing manually will never see a non-CV offer. No data is registered and no accept click happens, so nothing irreversible occurs, but if browsing non-CV offers becomes desirable the branch will need a switch guard.

findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MyAccessibilityService.kt lastClosedId dedupe skips retries after a successful click
findings.claim: lastClosedId is set only when the click returns true, so a failed click retries on the next event. If the click reports success but the popup does not actually close (for example a stale node), later events for the same id skip the close attempt and the popup stays open until the user dismisses it. This favors avoiding repeated clicks on an animating popup; recovery is manual and bounded to that one offer.
